entities.summary:
Thomas Grey, 2nd Marquess of Dorset (1477–1530), was an English Tudor magnate, grandson of Elizabeth Woodville’s first marriage line, who navigated the courts of Henry VII and Henry VIII. Holding Dorset and extensive midlands interests, he combined military service with the precarious politics of early Tudor nobility.

His career bridges Yorkist kinship residue and Henrician consolidation. Family ties later connected to the Grey claim through Lady Jane Grey’s line.

Dorset exemplifies early Tudor aristocratic survival and service.

His or its historical footprint survives in specialised scholarship, institutional memory, and the wider narrative structures through which later ages organised political, religious, and cultural experience across regions.
